name: Été Coffee
why_it_matters: Nagaland's first homegrown coffee-roasting company, founded 2016 by Lichan Humtsoe and his wife. Sources beans exclusively from four Nagaland districts — Kohima, Mokokchung, Mon and Wokha — and runs a stated 'Justice in a cup' ethics chain (no exploited growers, sustainable employment). The Billy Graham Road bar is the roastery flagship.
insider_tip: Ask which Nagaland district the day's pour-over is from — the Mon and Wokha lots taste very different from the Kohima beans. Billy Graham Road itself is a piece of trivia: built in 1972 for the only crusade Billy Graham held in Northeast India, this is the only road in the world named after him.

name: D Cafe
why_it_matters: Ranked #1 of 34 Kohima restaurants on Tripadvisor for several years running. Owner-roaster Dili Khekho keeps the menu deliberately tight — organic, fresh-roasted coffee beans, fresh-baked pastries, waffles. Wood-touch interiors, small terrace overlooking the Jail Colony road; dependable Wi-Fi makes it the de facto remote-work spot in Kohima.
insider_tip: Coffee comes out at café-grade — order an espresso or filter, not the milk-heavy options. Get there before 11am for the freshest pastry batch; the terrace fills up by mid-afternoon.

name: Sorshia & Co.
why_it_matters: P.R. Hill cafe with a strong Korean-Asian lean — Korean kimbap and noodles alongside stir-fried beef, pork ribs and sliders. Founders profiled by Roots and Leisure for putting their own spin on pan-Asian rather than copying Chinese-Naga staples. Cosy room, clear 'Kohima feels' design.
insider_tip: The kimbap and Korean noodles are what set it apart — most other Kohima cafes don't run those. Belho Complex on P.R. Hill — a 5-minute uphill walk from the Hotel Japfu side.

name: Dream Cafe
why_it_matters: Elevated cafe near the Commonwealth War Cemetery (one of Kohima's two WWII anchor sites — the Battle of Kohima cemetery). Window seats deliver what reviewers call a 'breathtaking glimpse of Kohima town.' Mixed Naga + continental menu; popular with the youth crowd for momos and pizza.
insider_tip: Service is famously slow — go for the view, not the speed. Pair it with a 30-minute walk through the Commonwealth War Cemetery just below: the WWII Battle of Kohima 'tennis-court' line is at the cemetery's centre.
signature_address: Sers Bazaar, TCP Gate, near Commonwealth War Cemetery, Kohima 797001

name: Ozone Cafe
why_it_matters: Long-running budget cafe at Main Market Junction — cited by MorungExpress as a Kohima foodie staple. Multi-cuisine (Chinese, continental, Naga) with momo as the headline. 509 online reviews, 3.9/5 — far cheaper than the Jail Colony spots, ₹200-400 for two.
insider_tip: Hours are tight — 11am to 5pm only, so this is a daytime stop, not dinner. Order the momos and the filter coffee; the burgers and pizza get inconsistent reviews.
signature_address: Dr Neilhouzhu Road, Block D, Kohima 797001

name: Fifa Cafe
why_it_matters: Casual cafe with a strong American/Chinese menu — Tripadvisor 4.2/5 (#7 of 18 Kohima restaurants on the older list), and a popular hangout for Kohima's college crowd. The newer 'Fifa Restaurant 2.0' offshoot runs the same kitchen template at higher capacity.
insider_tip: Bring a group — it's a hangout-style room, not a date spot. Order the fried chicken and milkshakes; that's what the regulars come for, not the pasta.

name: Cafe Aurora
why_it_matters: Razhu Point cafe with a pizza-and-momo menu and a few useful vegetarian options (sandwiches, soups) for travellers who want a break from smoked pork. Mid-tier on Tripadvisor (3.1/5, ranked #16 of 18), better-rated locally — Razhu Point itself is one of Kohima's main residential pockets.
insider_tip: Stick to the pizza and pork momo — the wider menu gets inconsistent reviews. Razhu Point is a useful stop if you're staying in that part of town and don't want to taxi to Jail Colony.
signature_address: Super Market Road, Razhu Point, Kohima 797001
